title: BotForje Configuration Schema (v1 draft)
description: Editor schema for BotForje YAML configuration. Draft v1: once generation from Go structs exists (ADR 0007) this file is generated and never edited by hand.

$schema.description: Points to this schema file for IDE autocompletion and validation

version.description: Schema version. Code uses this to select the correct parser. Increment when making incompatible changes.

default_timeout.description: Default graph session timeout in seconds

data_dir.description: Directory for the SQLite database; defaults to the XDG data directory

include.description: Glob patterns or file paths to fragment YAML files. Each fragment can define actions, graphs, and/or bots — any mix, any organization. Global settings are not allowed in fragments.

Fragment.description: Schema for included YAML fragment files. Only catalogs allowed — no global settings or include.

ActionCatalog.description: Map of action name to action definition

GraphCatalog.description: Map of graph name to graph definition

BotCatalog.description: Map of bot name to bot definition

ActionDefinition.description: A reusable action composed of sequential steps

scope.description: Optional isolation namespace. Defaults to 'default'. Entities in different scopes can share names and never reference each other

steps.description: Steps executed in sequence when the action triggers

Inputs.description: Named arguments for this tool. Steps consume them as {{input.<name>}}. An input may bind to a node or graph variable to read and write it

type.description: Value type expected from the agent

required.description: Whether the agent must provide this argument

default.description: Value used when the agent omits the argument

bind.description: Context variable this argument reads from and writes to, for example node.product; must be declared in initial_context

description.description: How the agent should fill this argument

Guards.description: Pre-execution guards that can block an action

duration.description: Seconds before the same sender can re-trigger this action

on_blocked.description: Steps to run when cooldown blocks the action

Step.description: One of: message (text reply), request (HTTP call), location (map pin)

message.description: Reply text. body only: deterministic. intent only: LLM realization with no fallback. body plus intent: LLM generates with body as anchor and sends body when generation is unavailable or the policy check fails

body.description: Deterministic reply text. With intent it is the factual anchor and the fallback. A list means random variants and is only allowed without intent

intent.description: What the reply should accomplish; short, clear text; enables LLM realization

policy.description: Optional refinement of the node policy for this reply; the node policy still applies. Requires intent

name.description: Identifier for this request; used in template resolution as {{node.name.resp.body.*}}

retry.description: Number of retry attempts on failure

GraphDefinition.description: A conversation state machine with named nodes and directed edges

scope.description: Optional isolation namespace. Defaults to 'default'. References resolve only within the same scope

timeout.description: Session TTL in seconds (overrides global default_timeout)

fallback.description: Node to route to when no edge matches

initial_context.description: Session context: free-form key-value pairs that persist across nodes; tools can bind inputs to these variables

nodes.description: Map of node name to node definition

NodeDefinition.description: A single graph state. Describes what the conversation is doing here and how it transitions

goal.description: What the agent must achieve in this state, short and clear; names the agent's objective, not a routing target

policy.description: Ambient constraints for the state: agent decisions, tool selection, and generated text

initial_context.description: Node context: free-form key-value pairs that reset every time the node is entered; tools can bind inputs to these variables

on_enter.description: Actions to run automatically when entering this node

on_exit.description: Actions to run automatically when leaving this node

tools.description: Actions the agent may invoke while in this node (ADR 0008); arguments are validated against each action's inputs

edges.description: Outgoing edges evaluated in order; first match wins

EdgeDefinition.description: A directed edge from one node to another. Every edge has a user-side intent, except the default (catch-all) edge, which has only goto. triggers is an optional deterministic fast path

intent.description: User trigger, short and clear text such as "wants a human"; required except on the default edge

triggers.description: Optional phrases that trigger this transition without the LLM; the match is fuzzy, so variations count too, and they double as classifier examples

BotDefinition.description: A bot instance that connects a transport (WhatsApp) to a graph

scope.description: Optional isolation namespace. Defaults to 'default'. The bot and its referenced graph must share the same scope

graph.description: Name of the graph this bot uses (must exist in the same scope)

allowed_senders.description: Whitelist of sender phone numbers; empty/null = all allowed

LLM.description: Language model integration. Optional: bots run deterministically with no provider configured. Draft shape; final details close in Phase 4/7

provider.description: Provider id, for example openai, anthropic, or ollama

model.description: Model name passed to the provider

api_key_env.description: Name of the environment variable holding the API key. Never store keys in config

base_url.description: Endpoint override for local or self-hosted providers

routing.description: Intent classification for input that matches no deterministic edge

realization.description: Whether nodes and messages that declare an intent may generate text

agent.description: Bounds for agentic tool use inside a node

max_tools_per_message.description: Maximum tool calls the agent may make for one incoming message
